A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A and B. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments in Figures 1–2 and TabPFN-v2 looping experiments on 17 OpenML datasets in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic experiments in Figures 1–2 and the tabular classification results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The attention architectures, propagation constructions, estimators, and LoopTabFM algorithm remain unchanged. Proposition 2's explicit looping qualification describes the existing construction rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic binary Gaussian-mixture scenarios and the same 17 OpenML binary classification datasets. No evaluated task, domain, or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain the same SPI/SSPI estimators and attention/Transformer comparisons. Table 1 retains the Loop-0 TabPFN-v2 baseline and Loop-1 through Loop-5. Newly cited TabDPT is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the synthetic dimensions, noise, training budgets, optimization settings, and accuracy metric. Tabular evaluations still use 10 labeled and 10 unlabeled examples, an 80% test split, and up to five loops.

E4.justification: The analyses of depth, unlabeled-sample availability, optimal mixing parameter alpha, architecture differences, and looping iterations are unchanged. Neither appendix adds an empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report maximum synthetic test accuracy over 10 random initializations and average tabular accuracy over 100 random trials/splits. No uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or reporting procedures are added.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 retain the same curves and findings, and all Table 1 entries are unchanged. Both tables report average accuracies of 68.84% for Loop-0 and 73.21% for Loop-5, with 6.35% relative improvement.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 now explicitly requires the single-layer model to be looped L times to reproduce Equation (11); v1 omitted this condition from the statement. This corrects the formal claim to match the existing shared-parameter construction. Appendix B.2's proof and the remaining theoretical results and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The main claims remain single-layer attention's inability to exploit unlabeled data, the benefits and polynomial expressivity of depth/looping, and improved tabular prediction through LoopTabFM. The abstract and concluding contribution claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The covariance-based explanations, EM/belief-propagation interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged. Both versions discuss the restriction to linear-attention theory and inconsistent tabular gains, including declines on OpenML datasets 31 and 40900.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, optimizer hyperparameters, sampling instructions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No new hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds concurrent work by Liu and Yang (2026), noting a similar observation but different model and data regimes. The introduction adds TabDPT (Ma et al., 2025), while the Kumar et al. (2020) and Xu et al. (2021) discussions and references are removed. These are limited updates to research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, grammar, notation, and bibliographic edits, including Proposition 2's wording, a prediction-symbol typo, and an added NJIT affiliation. The section order, overall narrative, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation line and revised related work and bibliography cause small layout and text-pagination shifts. Figures 1–2, Table 1, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, and placement; the appendices retain their layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by explicitly stating the looping requirement in Proposition 2 and improves context by acknowledging closely related concurrent work in Section 1.1. These are useful, limited improvements; the methods, empirical evidence, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.
